reasoning: This is a single-arm phase II trial with only 9 patients, making it severely underpowered for definitive conclusions. The 33.3% response rate (3/9 patients) suggests some biological activity, but without target engagement data or biomarkers, we cannot confirm if lapatinib engaged EGFR/HER2 or if the responses were due to the intended mechanism. The small sample size makes it impossible to distinguish between true efficacy and random variation. The serious GI safety signals (intestinal obstruction/perforation) are concerning but may be unrelated to the mechanism. Without a control arm or historical comparison, we cannot assess whether 33.3% represents meaningful activity above background.

failure_modes.evidence: Only 9 patients enrolled in a single-arm trial, far below typical phase II sample sizes needed for reliable efficacy assessment
No target engagement data, no biomarkers, no PK/PD data to confirm mechanism of action or assess causal chain
